newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Monti wants wide reform of EU transit regime.
newsitem.headline: Monti wants wide reform of EU transit regime.

text.p: Internal Market Commissioner Mario Monti said on Wednesday there was a need for a wide reform of the European Union's fraud-ridden transit regime.
Speaking to the European Parliament's Committee of Inquiry, Monti seemed to be in broad agreement with a draft committee report on customs fraud in the transit system.
"A far-reaching but well balanced reform is what we are both after," Monti said of the report, which is expected to be adopted by the committee on February 19 and debated in plenary session in March.

Monti acknowledged that the Commission shared part of the responsibility for developments in the transit system. For example, he said the Commission in its 1992 programme could have raised certain questions about the future of the transit system.
But, he added, "I'm not convinced that there is a direct link between the abolition of internal borders and the problems in the transit system."

The Commission was concerned because of the gap that exists between what has been agreed to in principle and what has actually been done in some member states, he said, adding that he would raise this point with EU finance ministers.

He said the extension of the EU's transit system on July 1 last year to the so called Visegrad countries of Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic and Slovakia had been a political choice and part of the pre-accession strategy.
It had not been disastrous as some people had feared, he said. But there would be no future extension until the transit system has been computerised.

The Commission and the European Court of Auditors estimate some 200 million European currency units are lost from the EU budget every year as a result of fraud against the system, notably relating to cigarettes, spirits and other goods subject to high duty rates.
